newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan names former judge to fight corruption.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan names former judge to fight corruption.

text.p: Pakistani President Farooq Leghari has named a former supreme court judge to head a new anti-corruption commission, an official said on Thursday.
Ghulam Mujadid Mirza, a former chief justice of the Lahore High Court and Supreme Court judge, was appointed to a four-year term as chief "ehtesab" (accountability) commissioner.

A presidential ordinance promulgated on Monday created the commission, which will receive corruption complaints against politicians and senior bureaucrats and refer them to high courts if it is satisfied that a prima facie case exists.

Leghari issued the decree 13 days after dissolving the National Assembly (lower house) and firing Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government on disputed charges of corruption, nepotism, misrule and extrajudicial killings.
The new ordinance will lapse after 90 days unless endorsed by a new assembly, to be elected on February 3 in polls supervised by a caretaker government led by Meraj Khalid.
Khalid has promised to bring unspecified charges against Bhutto and her husband, Asif Ali Zardari, who has been detained under a maintenance of public order law since November 5.
Politicians convicted under the ordinance are barred from standing for election.
